title: HCP — Get Entry — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Get entry operation (HCP 5.2.2): an HCP Client asks a provider for one named entry, for a stated purpose, under the grant its access token evidences. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty.

ref.description: HCP `ref`: the grant-scoped reference a Context Client was given when the entry was disclosed to it (HCP 5.2.2, 7.4). Exactly one of `ref` and `entryId` is present; that rule is not checked by the schema (a schema `oneOf` would complicate every generated library), and a request with both or neither fails with `malformedRequest`. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

entryId.description: HCP `entryId`: the entry's `id`, by which a Management Client names it (HCP 5.2.2). A Context Client never knows an entry's `id` (HCP 7.4).

purpose.description: HCP `purpose`: a purpose code the grant approved for a category of the entry (HCP 5.2.2, 6.1.5.2).

purposeDescription.description: HCP `purposeDescription`: a plain-language statement of the task, recorded in the provider's audit log (HCP 5.2.2, 8.2). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

version.description: HCP `version`: the entry version to return instead of the current one (HCP 5.2.2).

accessToken.description: The HCP access token for the grant under which the client acts (HCP 12, 13), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP Binding sends it as a Bearer token (HCP 9.3); this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

Response.title: HCP — Get Entry — response payload
Response.description: The HCP Get entry result (HCP 5.2.2): the entry, inside a result so that the minimization report has somewhere to sit. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

entry.description: HCP `entry`: a Disclosure where the requester is a Context Client (HCP 7.4), with its `useUntil` (HCP 7.6); otherwise the whole Entry.

retrievalId.description: HCP `retrievalId`: the `urn:uuid:` identifier of this retrieval, recorded in the `context.read` audit event (HCP 5.2.2, 8.2).

minimization.description: HCP `minimization`: the minimization report (HCP 7.5). Its `method` is `none`, since the caller named a single entry (HCP 5.2.2, 9.4.2).

directives.description: HCP `directives`: the directives that apply, where the requester is a Context Client (HCP 5.2.2, 6.4); empty when none applies. Null where the requester is not a Context Client, to whom HCP delivers no directives. HCP's own shape leaves the member optional; the carriage requires it, as a list or null, so that "none applies" is never confused with "not a Context Client", pending HCP confirmation (question 42).

respondedAt.description: HCP `timestamp`, renamed: the date-time of the response (HCP 5.2.2).
